Java 26, Maven 3.10.0. Let me set up a standard Maven project with SLF4J API and a runtime binding (Logback is a common choice). The user specifically wants a logging facade so app code isn't tied to a specific implementation. So use SLF4J API as compile dependency, and a runtime binding (Logback) as runtime scope.

- pom.xml
- src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java
- src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java maybe
- src/main/resources/logback.xml (runtime binding config)

Let me check the opencode.json to understand context maybe. Actually not necessary. Let me just build the project.

Let me use a reasonable groupId/artifactId. Since no name given, I'll use com.example:logging-demo. Java 26 - release 26? Maven compiler plugin supports release. But SLF4J 2.x. Let me check internet access? Maven will need to download dependencies. Let me try.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>logging-demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>logging-demo</name>
    <description>Maven Java project using SLF4J as the logging facade.</description>

    <properties>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
        <slf4j.version>2.0.16</slf4j.version>
        <logback.version>1.5.12</logback.version>
        <junit.version>5.11.4</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Logging facade: the only logging dependency application code compiles against. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Runtime binding. Scoped to runtime so it does not leak into compile classpath. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
            <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
            <version>${logback.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.13.0</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.2</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.0</version>
                <configuration>
                    <mainClass>com.example.app.App</mainClass>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

Everything works. Let me give a concise summary. The project structure:

- pom.xml: SLF4J API compile dep, Logback runtime dep, JUnit test dep
- src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java: uses org.slf4j.Logger
- src/main/resources/logback.xml: config
- src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java

One thing to mention: the runtime binding is scoped `runtime` so application code only compiles against SLF4J. Swapping implementations = replace that single runtime dependency.

Let me note the final tree briefly. Keep it short.

Done. Project structure:

```
pom.xml
src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java
src/main/resources/logback.xml
src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java
```

Key setup in `pom.xml`:
- `slf4j-api` — compile-scope facade; the only logging dependency app code compiles against.
- `logback-classic` — `runtime` scope binding, so it stays off the compile classpath.

`App.java:1` imports only `org.slf4j`; swapping implementations (Log4j2, JUL, etc.) means changing the single runtime dependency, not application code.

Verified: `mvn test` → BUILD SUCCESS (1 test), and `mvn exec:java` logs through Logback as configured in `logback.xml`.
